articleTitle: Estimation of Signal Distortion in Industrial Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Signal propagation in industrial scenario is characterized by strong reflections from metallic surfaces which causes multipath fading. This is generally means complex signal processing at receiver side which limits battery life of industrial devices. In this work it is proposed to consider propagation of single-frequency signals at warehouse using different pulse shapes and estimate signal distortion. It is shown that application of smoother pulse shapes leads to lower level of signal distortion in industrial scenario. Switching from rectangular pulse shape to half wave sine to the tenth power gives maximum error vector magnitude about 12% instead of 82%.

articleTitle: Effect of Electron Irradiation on Optical Properties of Sodium Silicate Glass with Silver, Copper and Gold Films
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: It has been experimentally shown that irradiation of silicate glasses with thin films of gold, silver and copper by electrons with energy E = 45 keV leads to the formation of neutral molecular clusters of metals and the appearance of luminescence in the irradiation region. Subsequent heat treatment leads to the quenching of luminescence due to the formation from nanocluster of gold, silver and copper nanoparticles that have plasmon resonance in the visible region of the spectrum.

Index Terms: Increase In The Intensity Of Band

articleTitle: Modification of the Adaptive Moving Average Filter for the Signal Parameters Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Moving average filters are among the most popular types of filters used in measuring transducers in the electric power grid. Adaptive modification (with adjustment of the filter length to the interference frequency) allows achieving high measurement accuracy the root mean square value, active power, and reactive power for appropriate measurement methods of these parameters. However, in order to achieve high metrological accuracy, it is necessary to either increase the sampling rate or cascade several identical or different filter stages. The first approach leads to an increase in the computational load on the digital signal processing device used in the implementation. The second one leads to an increase in the filter setting time, which leads to an increase in the dynamic component of the error. In this paper, we consider an alternative approach to the problem, known as the "vernier" method. This method involves approximating the signal for the final sampling step over the entire averaging time. We consider the application of zero-order, first-order, and second-order polynomials, and propose algorithms for their practical implementation. Additionally, we propose variants for constructing simulation models of filters to estimate the error caused by incomplete interference filtering. The magnitude response of the modified moving average filter have been performed, and an assessment of the implementation complexity has been appreciated.

articleTitle: Computer Simulation of Alanine Oligomers in an IR Electric Field with Different Form and Polarization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: A method of computer simulation of intramolecular vibrations of alanine oligomers in an electric field possesses different types of polarization. Amplitude-time realizations of the integral electric dipole moment of biomolecules and the Fourier spectrum of frequencies of intramolecular vibrations were calculated. Effects of changes in spectral components in the far and middle IR ranges were identified, which reveal physical properties and transformations of the states of biomolecules due to differences in polarization of the irradiating field. The obtained data can be used in life sciences, in various spectroscopic studies, and in the development of medical, pharmaceutical, and nano-biomolecular technologies, as well as in bioelectronic and heterogeneous hybrid microelectronic devices with embedded biomolecular components.

articleTitle: Development of Lamination-Based Technological Approach for Encapsulation of Ionic EAP Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Sensors and actuators based on ionic electroactive polymers have a set of properties that are useful in biomedicine. There is an important problem of maintaining the performance of sensors made of ionic polymer-polymer and ionic polymermetal composites. To solve this problem, sensor encapsulation methods are used, due to which the electrolyte is retained inside the sensor membrane for a long time. However, not all encapsulation methods are effective and feasible for industrial production of sensors based on electroactive polymers. This work proposes a lamination-based technological approach for encapsulating such sensors using inexpensive materials. The developed approach consists of 5 technological operations and significantly increases the lifetime and stability of the manufactured sensors. The characteristics of encapsulated sensors with different geometric parameters were studied. The output signal of the 5.5 mm long encapsulated sensor decreased by 2% in 2.5 hours (sensor thickness − 0.4 mm).

articleTitle: Picosecond Laser with Yb-doped Tapered Double Clad Fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In this study, we present results of development fiber picosecond laser by using an active ytterbium tapered double clad optical fiber with mode field diameter of 35 µm and low intrinsic birefringence (1.45×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup> rad/m). We have demonstrated 1040nm/50ps optical source with tunable repetition rate (within range of 1-20 MHz) and an average power of 160 W (peak power 160 kW, 8 µJ per pulse) delivering Gaussian beam with excellent quality (M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> ~ 1.11/1.22).

articleTitle: Measuring the Noise Figure of a Cooled Broadband Radio Astronomy Receiver
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: A method for measuring the noise figure of a radioastronomical receiver at low temperatures achieved by using a compact Stirling-type cooler is presented. The proposed method combines the classical scalar Y-factor method with measurements of the S-parameters of receiver scattering matrix using a vector network analyzer. The results of measuring the receiver noise figure and S-parameters in the frequency band from 3 to 18 GHz and in the temperature range from 300 K to 148 K are given

articleTitle: Low-Complexity Nonlinear Hybrid Precoding for Massive MIMO Broadcast Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Nonlinear hybrid precoding can approach capacity, but is highly computational. This paper investigates a low-complexity nonlinear hybrid precoding algorithm designed to maximize the achievable sum-rate of massive multiple-input multiple-output broadcast channels (MIMO-BC). We propose a closed-form solution for the analog precoding design to reduce the computational complexity of nonlinear hybrid precoding. The key idea is to transform the intractable constant modulus problem into an equivalent unconstrained problem by treating the phases as optimization variables, which can be efficiently solved using the Fletcher-Reeves conjugate gradient method. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm achieves near-optimal sum-rate performance while maintaining computational efficiency, with complexity scaling linearly with the number of transmit antennas, making it highly competitive in massive MIMO systems.

articleTitle: Effect of Gamma and Electron Irradiation on the Spectral and Luminescent Properties of a Composite Film with Halide Perovskite Nanocrystals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper presents the results of a study of an optical composite with a glass-crystalline filler exposed to ionizing radiation. The glass-crystalline material consists of a borosilicate matrix in which CsPbBr3 nanocrystals were formed as a result of heat treatment. The spectral and luminescent properties of composite films exposed to gamma and electron irradiation were assessed. The results obtained indicate that the composite retains the emissivity of halide perovskite nanocrystals, while the observed decrease in the integral transmittance after electron irradiation with fluence 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sup> e/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> did not exceed 5 %.

articleTitle: Research of Deformation of Concrete Structures Using Fiber Optic Sensors and Bragg Gratings
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This research proposes a new method for monitoring the condition of concrete structures using fiber Bragg gratings (FBG) sensors. These sensors, specifically designed to minimize damage during concrete placement, provide the ability to monitor concrete deformation in real-time, which is a key factor for concrete strengthening and structural safety. Laboratory tests have demonstrated the high accuracy and reliability of Bragg grating sensors in measuring static and dynamic loads, temperature deformations, and the detection and development of micro-cracks. The use of Bragg gratings allows for modeling the technical characteristics of concrete, predicting its strength, and increasing the safety of construction projects. The results obtained confirm the effectiveness of Bragg gratings in monitoring the condition of structures, which makes them an important tool in modern construction and engineering. This method helps to reduce construction-related risks such as crack initiation and subsequent structural failure, thus improving condition monitoring of buildings, bridges, and other concrete structures.

articleTitle: Growing of Biomolecular Micro Particles and Surface Films with Ultrasound Activation of Solution
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This study introduces an innovative ultrasonic spraying technique for the rapid formation of both biomolecular microparticle beams in the atmospheric pressure air, and films on various substrates. By deploying amino acid solutions at atmospheric pressure and ambient temperatures, we achieved the deposition of microparticles forming structured films with diverse morphologies, such as compact rings and microcrystalline pellets. These particles were observed on a substrate in kind of ring and pellets structures with an average size of approximately 100 micrometers, which demonstrated potential features for high number internal degrees of freedom and spatial-energetic states. The application of this technology spans biomedicine, microelectronics, and nanophotonics, where precise biomolecular assemblies are crucial. Initial results suggest that these biomolecular films could also serve as biofunctional and electromagnetic components in advanced nanostructured materials, paving the way for new integrative approaches in hybrid microelectronics and photonics.

articleTitle: A Joint Estimation Algorithm of Timing and Carrier under Large Frequency Offset Satellite Signal
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: For low-orbit satellite communication systems, it is necessary to synchronize the received signals and estimate the frequency offset. Using chirp and Unique Words, a joint timing and carrier estimation algorithm can be completed. This algorithm can accurately estimate the Doppler frequency shift of low-orbit satellites, and is an algorithm that can meet the requirements of positioning and estimating frequency offset under high-speed motion. Through the joint algorithm, the signals from low-orbit satellites are synchronized at high speed and the frequency offset is estimated, and pass into the negative feedback loop to eliminate the Doppler frequency offset in time.

articleTitle: Signal Distortions in Switched Mode Power Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The causes of signal distortions are given and observed when using switched-mode power amplifiers (PA) for amplifying signals with high PAPR. Distortion causes in RF and envelope PAs are given. For example, in RF PA distortions are mostly caused by the output network and time characteristics of the transistor. For L. Kahn schematic, the envelope PA distortion estimation of AM-AM characteristic based on transistors’ non-ideal time characteristics is represented. The parameters mostly responsible for distortions appearance are determined.

articleTitle: Sorting Algorithms in Switching-Based Calibration of DACs with Non-Ideal Comparator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper is devoted to the research of sorting algorithms in switching-based calibration of DACs. Switching-based calibration employs a comparator and elements sort to detect actual values of elements. In real calibration circuits, the comparator is non-ideal and has a finite threshold. The latter one leads to wrong comparator decisions and an appearance of error in sort phase. This research investigates influence of a threshold on the sort phase and its subsequent contribution to integral nonlinearity for arrays with random errors. Simulation shows that the best results are demonstrated by a selection sort, which provides a sorting error and INL less than other sorting algorithms.

articleTitle: Self-Assembled InGaAs Quantum Dots with Reduced Inhomogeneous Broadening
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The results on fabrication by molecular-beam epitaxy of self-assembled InGaAs quantum dots using the Stranski–Krastanow growth mode are presented. Temperature study of photoluminescence spectra has shown that quantum dots assembled from the In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.45</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.55</inf>As layer have reduced inhomogeneous broadening compared to quantum dots formed from the InGaAs layer with a larger indium content.

articleTitle: Development and Validation of LTE SDR-based Signal Analyzer. Part 1. Procedures Description
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The purpose of the work is to realize and validate the procedures of LTE physical layer, required for signal analyzer to operate and solve positioning task in conditions of inaccessibility of global navigation satellite systems. From the analysis of open sources it follows, that this study is the first work, that describes in detail the procedures for analyzing broadcast signals of the LTE standard to determine the location of software-defined radio (SDR) based user equipment (UE). Practical significance of the proposed solution is LTE SDR-based signal analyzer, allowing to determine the location of a UE, being not a network subscriber, with the accuracy of proximity to the nearest cell.

articleTitle: Ship Detection in SAR Images Using Neural Network Trained on Optical Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper discusses automated ship detection in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images by a neural network (NN) trained on grayscale optical images. It is shown that good detection quality can be achieved using this approach despite significant differences between radar and optical images. Since, unlike optical images, SAR images are always corrupted by strong multiplicative speckle noise, several speckle noise reduction filters were applied to SAR images before detection. Different filters have significantly varying effect on detection quality. NN based noise reduction filters outperformed traditional types (Lee filter, Frost filter, etc,). NN noise reduction filters were trained using grayscale optical images with artificial speckle noise.

articleTitle: Pulse Electrical Strength of Polymer Dielectric Films
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The pulsed electrical strength of PP and PET films has been investigated. It has been established that the breakdown of these films is possible both at the front and at the plateau of the pulse. A jump in the durability of the films has been recorded during the transition from breakdown at the front to breakdown at the plateau of the pulse. It has been shown that the processes preparing the electric breakdown of the films develop faster at the front, and not at the plateau of the pulse. A possible physical mechanism explaining this effect has been discussed.

articleTitle: Ring Cavity Surface-Emitting Quantum-Cascade Lasers with Staircase-like Distributed Feedback Grating
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The results on fabrication and experimental study of ring cavity surface-emitting quantum-cascade lasers with staircase-like distributed feedback grating are presented. The grating with a gradient in etching depth of the slits along the ring cavity was formed by direct high-vacuum ion-beam lithography. The lasing was observed close to 7.9 μm at 293 K with maximum output power about 15 mW. Analysis of the near and far field patterns showed that created ring quantum-cascade lasers operated on a high order transverse mode.

articleTitle: MIMO-NOMA Analysis. Part I. Beamforming
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This study is devoted to the characteristics of MIMO systems with non-orthogonal multiple access. In this part of the work, a comparative analysis of digital and hybrid methods for obtaining a multipath radiation pattern for a downstream data flow is carried out.

articleTitle: The Effect of the Slot in Wave Propagation: Theoretical and Experimental Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper investigates the wave propagation characteristics through vertical slots in both free space and within rectangular waveguides. Numerical simulations are conducted to model wave transmission through the slot under different conditions, and experimental measurements are performed to validate the results. The findings reveal that while the transmitted power through the slot remains constant, the resonant frequencies differ between free-space and waveguide environments due to the computational models not accounting for the reactive impedance of the slot. The study emphasizes the importance of calculating the reactive impedance of slots to improve the accuracy of wave propagation models. This information is crucial for applications in array antennas and phase shifter technologies, where precise control of wave characteristics is required. The results provide a foundation for enhancing the performance of future communication and radar systems.

articleTitle: Simulation of the Active Filter Tuning Systems Based on Delay Times, Periods and Phases Comparison
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In this paper is described an auto tuning methods of active RC filters. The tuning range and the tuning accuracy are analyzed. To verify the method, analog and digital part of the tuning system are cosimulated together. The simulation results shows that the time constant tuning accuracy is ±3.8% for tuning circuit based on delay times comparison, 5.5% for circuit based on period comparison and 3.9% for tuning circuit based on phase comparison by 4-bit code sequence and time-constant variation ±28%.

articleTitle: Design of a MEMS Accelerometer in COMSOL Multiphysics and a Pickup Circuit Model in Matlab Simulink
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In this study, multiple models of the sensing element for a capacitive accelerometer were developed, and a preliminary analysis was conducted to assess the alignment of the first natural frequencies along the x and y axes. Models exhibiting discrepancies in their first frequencies relative to these axes were excluded due to non-compliance with the requirement for low cross-sensitivity. Consequently, two models with a sufficient separation of natural frequencies along the x and y axes, compared to other axes, were selected. The transfer functions for displacement/acceleration and capacitance/displacement were identified as key characteristics for integrating the models into Matlab SIMULINK software. Given that the natural frequencies of the sensing element significantly exceed the maximum frequency of the measured signal, the frequency-dependent transmission characteristics were neglected. A single differential capacitance model was employed to simulate the capacitance-displacement relationship. Under an acceleration of 15g, the output signal from the accelerometer was measured at 276 mV.

articleTitle: Analysis of the State of Polarization at the Output of an Imperfect Faraday Rotator Mirror
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the polarization state transformations performed by imperfect Faraday rotator mirrors. By modeling the system with arbitrary birefringence in the connecting fiber, we derive the possible output polarization states. Leveraging Jones matrices, complex polarization variables, and Poincare sphere representations, we achieve a comprehensive understanding of the polarization transformations induced by imperfect Faraday rotator mirrors. These results are critical for optimizing fiber-optic systems that depend on precise polarization control and for developing robust testing methodologies to ensure reliable system performance.

articleTitle: Search, Estimate, and Predict: Efficient Weakly-Supervised Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Most of state-of-the-arts region-based detectors are suffered from the requirement of training for a large volume of bounding box annotated data. In this paper, we propose an innovative weakly-supervised architecture, namely SEP-Net, that employs an efficient proposal searching method on feature maps to generate region proposals via transforming CNN classifiers to object detectors without bounding box annotations. We further show the proposed framework can be used for real-time detection, in which high computation efficiency is a prerequisite. Moreover, the training procedure is exactly the same as what’s for CNN classifiers, so is easy to transfer a pre-trained CNN to our weakly-supervised detector as well. Experimental validation on ImageNet 2012 dataset show that the novel model outperforms classical and most recent state-of-the-art weakly-supervised method by a wide margin in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Current Pulse Generator for Deep Brain Stimulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Realization of a current driver is presented. It provides a stable current amplitude required for electrical stimulation devices. It is possible to increase the output impedance of the current driver as high as possible, that improves the stability of the output current with load resistance variation. However, achieving excessively high output impedances is pointless, as it will not lead to the desired current stabilization due to the presence of a noise current. In this case, the circuit of the current driver becomes unsalable, the chip area grows and power consumption increases. An algorithm for estimating the rational value of the current driver output impedance based on the RMS noise current at the output of the circuit is proposed. The presence of the output impedance limitation relaxes the size requirements of the current driver MOS transistors and its operational amplifier gain. The proposed algorithm is verified by circuit and layout level simulation using 180 nm CMOS technology.

articleTitle: System Level IC Analog Processing Design For Piezoresistive MEMS Pressure Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper presents an electronic readout integrated circuit (IC) design for a piezoresistive MEMS pressure sensor, based on system level approach. The system level approach provides key parameter evaluation in early design stage and system verification at later stages, thus reducing development time and cost. The electronic readout model consists of an instrumentation amplifier, low-pass filter and MASH ∑∆-modulator. The focus of this work is to find the optimal dynamic parameters of the analog signal processing circuit for achieving different levels of pressure sensor inaccuracy. The simulation results demonstrated that sensor inaccuracy of 0.05% due to electronic readout can be achieved by SFDR of 61 dB and SNR of 70.4 dB.

articleTitle: Refractive Index Measurement Resolution of the Core-Cladding Intermode Fiber Optic Interferometer with Spectral Interrogation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In this paper the intermodal fiber optic interferometer with the standard SMF-28 single-mode optical fiber which acts as a sensing element is considered. The calculation of the refractive index measurement resolution was performed using the Cramer-Rao relation. For that the sensitivities of the cladding mode propagation constants to the refractive index of surrounded media and the calculation of the cladding mode attenuation coefficients were carried out using numerical simulation. It has been found that the resolution increases for higher order modes and has a monotonic increasing character with increasing length of the sensitive section for the range up to several meters.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Electrophysical Properties of Composite Materials Based on Wollastonite and Bacterial Cellulose
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The technology of obtaining samples of wollastonite and composite material based on wollastonite and bacterial cellulose is described. The results of measuring the mechanical tensile strength, capillary absorbency and the tangent of the dielectric loss angle are presented. It is shown that the addition of wollastonite particles increases the capillary absorbency of the composite several times, but reduces its mechanical strength similar to the case of adding nanofillers to cellulose materials. It has been found that the addition of particles of some types of wollastonite reduces dielectric losses in the material.

articleTitle: Titanium-Indiffused Lithium Niobate Waveguides for Quantum Integrated Optical Circuits Working on the Wavelength of 808 nm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The technology for fabrication of titanium-indiffused optical waveguides working on the wavelength of 808 nm was elaborated. Experimental samples of waveguides on z-cut lithium niobate substrates were fabricated. Technological conditions providing their single-mode regime of operation were determined. Optical fiber-to-fiber losses of 1.9 dB for straight 20-mm-long waveguides for TM mode were measured. Modes of waveguides were captured, the propagation and coupling losses were estimated. The elaborated technology for producing waveguides can be further used to fabricate more complex integrated optical circuits operating at a wavelength of 808 nm, which is preferred for quantum applications such as quantum communications and quantum computing.

articleTitle: Features of Differential Current-Voltage Characteristics of Tunnel Structures Based on PbTe:In Single Crystals at Low Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The current-voltage characteristics of metal-insulator-semiconductor tunnel contacts based on bulk lead telluride single crystals doped with indium with an impurity content of 2 at. % were investigated at low temperatures (T < 40 K). The features of the differential conductivity of the contacts and its derivative associated with the indium impurity were analyzed. The hysteresis of the differential conductivity with a change in the sweep direction of a bias voltage is associated with metastable states on impurities at T < 20 K. The features of the current-voltage characteristics associated with the appearance of forced oscillations in the energy of band states in the subcontact region of the semiconductor were discovered. These oscillations appear when the lifetime of nonequilibrium impurity states approaches the period of bias voltage modulation oscillations. A phase analysis was performed, and the temperature dependences of such features of the differential characteristics were studied. The results made it possible to estimate the energy position of the single-electron impurity center-above the Fermi level position by ≈ 35 meV. Independent confirmation of predominantly paired electron filling of impurity states of indium-a impurity center with negative correlation energy has been obtained.

articleTitle: Design of a Class E Power Amplifier with Complex Impedance Load
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: A complex load class-E power amplifier (PA) analysis of optimal voltage and current waveforms and matching network algorithm are presented and verified by simulation in the time and frequency domain with 50% duty ratio. The designed PA exhibits high-efficiency characteristics of 89% drain efficiency.

articleTitle: Carbon Dots and Carbon Spheres produced by Hydrothermal Synthesis of Oligochitosan Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Porous carbon spheres with sizes ranging from tens to thousands of nanometers and luminescent carbon nanodots, which size is smaller than 10 nm can be produced by hydrothermal synthesis of dilute polymer solutions. Using natural polymers as the source for carbon dots and carbon spheres is promising from the ecological point of view. Both types of carbon structures are interesting for applications, but the phase separation into carbon spheres and carbon nanodots during the hydrothermal synthesis has not been studied. In this work, the products of hydrothermal treatment of dilute solutions of the water soluble oligomer of natural polysaccharide chitosan were studied. The absorption and luminescence spectra of carbon nanodots, and the scanning electron microscopy of carbon spheres were investigated. With increasing the synthesis duration, the degree of carbonization of both components, as well as the size of carbon spheres increase. It is shown for the first time that the quantum yield and luminescence linewidth of carbon nanodots depend on the filling degree of the autoclave.

articleTitle: Phonon Coherent States in Nanomaterials
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In our work we describe the heat transfer in nanomaterial by thermal excitations with accounting phonon coherent states. General second-quantization formalism for a time dependent problem for thermal conductivity is proposed. This method accounts both the usual phonon model of heat transfer and the formation of coherent Schrödinger states in each mode of the phonon system. An exact general form of solution with arbitrary initial conditions is analytically obtained. It is shown that at certain ratios of the interaction constants of phonons with the electronic subsystem a heat flow does not decay with time in the crystal that determines a heat superconductivity phenomenon

articleTitle: Application of Deep Learning for Classification of CT Images in Order to Predict EGFR and KRAS Mutations in Oncology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This study explores the application of advanced deep learning models to classify lung cancer tumors based on CT images into three groups: mutant EGFR, mutant KRAS, and wildtype. Utilizing a comprehensive radiogenomic dataset from 211 patients, we developed models using YOLOv10 and convolutional neural networks like ResNet and DenseNet to analyze and predict genetic mutations directly from CT scans. The results demonstrate high precision and recall in mutation detection, particularly for EGFR, with the potential to significantly enhance non-invasive diagnostic methods. This approach promises to improve clinical decision-making and treatment planning by providing rapid, accurate assessments of mutation status, thereby facilitating personalized therapy strategies in oncology.

articleTitle: Algorithms for Artificial Neural Networks with Interval Target Tuning for the Task of Classifying Cammeo and Osmancik Rice Varieties
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper investigates the application of intelligent learning algorithms for artificial neural networks (ANN) with interval target tuning for the task of classifying Cammeo and Osmancik rice varieties. The data used includes 3810 rice grain samples for which seven morphological features were measured. The core concept of the method is the creation of a multi-level hierarchical network consisting of various typical ANN modules interacting in a hierarchical structure based on a specially developed algorithm. The process of network synthesis and training is conducted, and the effectiveness of the proposed approach is analyzed. The results show that this method allows achieving high classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Multistage Energy Recovery in the SPbPU Gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Measurements have been carried out in a 4-mm wavelength gyrotron with a multi-stage depressed collector based on spatial separation of electrons in crossed axial electric and azimuthal magnetic fields. The results of the first experiments are discussed, in which the values of the total efficiency of ~ 70% for a four-stage and ~ 72% for a five-stage recuperation system were achieved. Suggestions for further increasing the gyrotron efficiency are proposed.

articleTitle: Comparison of Structure, Transport Properties and Thermoelectric Power Efficiency of Thin CrSi and CoSi Films on Si(111) and Si(100) Substrates
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper compares the formation conditions, crystal structure, conductivity, and thermoelectric properties of thin CrSi and CoSi films on silicon substrates with (111) and (100) orientations. It is found that, despite the insufficiently good conductivity, the films have a noticeable Seebeck coefficient (up to 70 μV/K) in the temperature range of 200-450 K: positive for CrSi and negative for CoSi. The maximum power factor is estimated at 2 to 3 mW/(m2×K). For CoSi, first-principles calculations of the phonon structure and lattice thermal conductivity are performed, including in the form of nanowires. Estimates are made for the achievable dimensionless thermoelectric figure of merit of CoSi thin films: ZT=0.40–0.50 T=200-450 K.

articleTitle: Histogram-Based Estimation of CIR Entropy for Multipath Propagation Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper considers a problem of accurate estimation of information entropy of wireless channel parameters for finite-size samples. Of a particular interest is the entropy of the Channel Impulse Response (CIR) in multipath environments. Multipath propagation characterized by a variety of signal paths due to random reflections, diffraction and scattering, induces a significant uncertainty in wireless channels, which affects the signal quality and system performance. We propose a new method for estimating the differential entropy of basic channel parameters, such as the multipath delay and amplitude of partial waves, using a histogram-based approach. An influence of the propagation environment parameters on the channel uncertainty is analyzed through a computer simulation, and the principal tradeoffs associated with the entropy estimation are identified. Our results provide an insight on the performance gain of CIR-based techniques in relation to the tasks of physical layer security.

articleTitle: Modification of Dielectric Properties of Polyvinyl Alcohol Films Using Water-Soluble Additives
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The purpose of the work is to find out dielectric characteristics of samples of polyvinyl alcohol and composites based on it in the frequency range below 100 Hz. In this work, films based on polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) with the addition of sodium chloride and fullerenol were fabricated, and the frequency dependences of dielectric permittivity, dielectric loss, and dissipation factor in the range of 0.01 – 100 Hz were measured and analyzed.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of 8K Display Chip Technology Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Currently, 4K Ultra High Definition (UHD) televisions have become mainstream, while 8K UHD display technology which represents the future of television, is rapidly developing. To carry out underlying technological innovation of 8K UHD display and develop differentiated high-end 8K display products, this paper presents the design and implementation of an 8K display chip technology platform. This platform integrates multiple mainstream 8K high-speed video interfaces and two sets of DDR4 high-speed memory, featuring 8K@60Hz signal processing capability. It also supports 8K@120Hz signal processing through dual-platform homogeneous computing technology. Therefore, this platform can simultaneously meet the R&D requirements for 8K@60Hz and 8K@120Hz display technologies, which has great significance for the innovation of underlying technologies in 8K UHD displays. Utilizing this platform, we designed a 230,400 partition Mini-LED backlight LCD display system, achieving a peak brightness of 5,420 nits and exceptional visual fidelity, thereby establishing a robust foundation for realistic HDR effects.

articleTitle: Reception Energy Loss of GMSK-Modulated Signals with a Narrow Frequency Band and a High Message Rate
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The growing number of participants in AIS systems leads to an overload of existing communication channels. One of the methods to solve the problem within the existing framework is to increase the data rate of messages. This article describes methods for increasing the transmission rate of GMSK signals at low values of the normalized frequency band. Using simulation, it is proved that the developed correlation algorithm has an energy gain equal to 1 dB with a narrow frequency band (ΔFT=0.3). The main result is an algorithm that increases the transmission rate of GMSK signals by approximately 2 times with a normalized frequency bandwidth of 0.3 under the conditions of a spectral mask's presence.

articleTitle: Intermodal Fiber Interferometer Based on an SMSMS structure with Spectral Interrogation for Measuring External Impacts
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: An intermodal fiber interferometer based on the SMSMS structure, with spectral interrogation and Fourier analysis of the signals, has been experimentally studied. It has been shown that such a scheme can be considered a sensor for external impacts with two sensitive sections, which are multimode fibers of different lengths. In this paper, the Fourier analysis method of the output signals of such a scheme was used to extract information about external impacts on two sensitive sections. It is shown that external impacts can be measured by obtaining the Fourier image of the spectral transfer function and finding the phases of the spectral components corresponding to two multimode fibers. The results of measuring the external impacts using the proposed approach are presented. It is shown that the proposed approach provides independent measurements of external impacts exerted on two multimode fibers, which are sensitive elements in an intermodal fiber interferometer based on the SMSMS structure.

articleTitle: Increasing the Noise Immunity of Communication Systems by Highly Directional Antennas Based on an Air Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper considers the design of two patch antennas based on an air substrate. The proposed antenna designs are aimed at implementing a noise-immune data transmission channel with highly mobile automated complexes. Proposed antenna designs have a fan-shaped radiation pattern, and have an isolated feed line layer for improved matching, directional properties. Thus, it was noted that the use of the proposed antenna design increases the noise immunity of communication channels

articleTitle: Preparation Of VO2 Thin Films On 6H-SiC Substrate By Magnetron Sputtering
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Experimental results of vanadium dioxide film deposition on silicon carbide substrate are presented in this article. The study of the crystal structure and surface characteristics showed the high quality of the vanadium dioxide film.The obtained samples demonstrate a phase transition of more than 4 orders of magnitude and IR radiation modulation by 22.3%.

articleTitle: Compensation’s Method of Collector Load’s Parasitic Components in SiGe and SOI Cascode Amplifiers Operating at High Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper considers the circuit method for neutralizing the effect of parasitic components of the collector load in silicon-germanium (SiGe) and silicon-on-insulator (SOI) classical cascade amplifiers and common-base stages on their voltage gain (Gain). The article demonstrates that the incorporation of a dedicated compensating circuit into the original circuits enables the enhancement of their upper frequency limit or gain by a factor of 5 to 10. The conditions for mitigating the impact of resistor parasites, which contribute to losses in planar inductance, on the Q-factor of the RLC-circuit of the selective amplifier are established. It is recommended that the proposed circuit solutions be employed in practical applications involving SiGe and SOI analog chips operating at elevated temperatures.

articleTitle: Anisotropy of Minority Charge Carrier Concentration in the MOSFET Undergate Region
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper considers the possibility of reducing nonlinear distortions of the active region of the current-voltage characteristic of a MOSFET by creating anisotropy in the silicon undergate region. The simulation of the technological process for creating such a region by ion implantation of boron with a dose of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>. Electron distributions in the channel and their change depending on the depth are obtained. In the operating mode, the anisotropy region narrows the conductive channel to several nanometers, which reduces the flowing current, at the same time complicates the process of electron injection with a further increase in the drain-source voltage, which increases the stability of the current-voltage characteristic in the active region.

articleTitle: The Influence of the Tips Geometry on the Formation of Electron Velocities in the Electron Flow
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Field emitters are advantageous in vacuum electron beam devices due to their lack of heating requirements. The study focuses on the impact of tip geometry on electron beam velocities and emission characteristics. It examines how the height of the tip, the radius of curvature, and the number of tips in multitip cathodes affect the spatial distribution of longitudinal and transverse electron velocities. These factors are crucial for optimizing the performance of electron beam devices, where precise control over electron beam characteristics is essential for efficiency and functionality.

articleTitle: Development and Validation of LTE SDR-based Signal Analyzer. Part 2. Experiment Results
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The purpose of work is software implementation and experimental testing of an LTE standard signal analyzer using a software-defined radio (SDR) for positioning with the accuracy of cell coverage. The main result is developed for a signal analyzer of the LTE standard in MATLAB, which implements the reception, processing and extraction of the necessary system information blocks, transmitted by base stations of the LTE standard via broadcast channels. The software interface is configured to work with the USRP B210 board. During experimental testing, system information blocks were received and processed from the air, extracting identifiers of operator base stations and then accessing the OpenCellID database to obtain global coordinates. From the analysis of open sources it follows, that this study is the first work, that describes the procedure for analyzing broadcast signals of the LTE standard to determine the location of user SDR device, being not a subscriber of any network, with the accuracy of proximity to the nearest cell in conditions of inaccessibility of global navigation satellite systems.

articleTitle: High-Quality General Method of Sub-Nyquist BandPass Sampling with Selected Minimal In-Band Distortion including Intermodulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: High-Quality BandPass Sampling of radio signals with Selected Minimal In-band Distortions including Intermodulation (HQBSSMDI) is highly demanded and very relevant both in various new studies and in the creation and design of many modern electronic devices, as well as in frequency planning with full clear the spectrum of harmonics distortion and intermodulation in the specified maximum frequency band.

articleTitle: Influence of a Miniature Gas Cell Heater on the Parameters of a Radio-Optical Resonance Line
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper presents the results of a study of the influence of the magnetic field generated by two types thin-film resistive bifilar heaters of a miniature gas cell, with single-layer and double-layer topologies, on the parameters of the radio-optical resonance line. The heaters were manufactured using MEMS technology. The influence of the heater magnetic field was estimated by the broadening and shifting of the radio-optical resonance line in <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">87</sup>Rb and <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">133</sup>Cs vapors during the operation of the experimental setup in the quantum magnetometer mode with optical pumping. It was shown, that when the heaters operate on direct current, the resonance line broadens by ~ 1.5 times for single-layer heater and by 1,05 times for double-layer heater. The use of the heaters on alternating current made it possible to completely eliminate the influence of the heater magnetic field on the resonance line parameters. The double-layer heater had a significantly smaller effect on the resonance line than the single-layer heater.

articleTitle: Moving Target Localization and Enclosing Control with Fixed-Wing Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This work tackles the problem of localizing and controlling fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) to enclose an unknown moving target. Each fixed-wing UAV only measures the distance to the target. An information filter is proposed to target localization via measured distance. Following this, an enclosing control law is developed to direct the fixed-wing UAV along a shared circular path with a target-centered, called motion planning. To do this, the fixed-wing UAV has a spatial temporal curve, which integrates two types of motion: tracking the trajectory of the target and maneuvering along the circular path around the target. The stability of the closed-loop system, incorporating the proposed estimation and enclosing control, is rigorously analyzed. Comprehensive computer simulations in two-dimensional settings are used to illustrate the strategy’s effectiveness.

articleTitle: Structural and Magnetic Phase Transitions in Gd5-x-yTbxTiySi2Ge2 Compounds
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Temperature studies of crystal structure of compounds based on Gd5Si2Ge2 doped with Tb and Ti were conducted. All compositions exhibited a temperature-induced structural phase transition from an orthorhombic structure to a monoclinic one. The crystal lattice parameters and volume changes during this phase transition were measured. The change in magnetic entropy, cooling capacity, and operational range of the magnetocaloric material were calculated for the studied compound. It was found that the efficiency of the material increased with the addition of Ti.

articleTitle: Design of a Digital RISC-V ASIC Using an Open-Source Software and Domestic Standard Cell Libraries
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In this article physical design flow of digital integrated circuits based on domestic standard cell library with an open-source software is considered. The main difficulties encountered in the interaction of the open-source software and the standard cell library are considered. The proposed ways of solving these difficulties are tested by carrying out logical synthesis and place-and-route for the three RISC-V microprocessor cores: «Ibex», «SweRV» and «SCR1».

articleTitle: A Model for Assessment of Nonlinear Phonon Drag Contribution to Thermopower in Metal/Semiconductor Nanocontacts
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: We propose a simple 1D model for estimating the "hidden" thermopower produced in nanocontacts, which is usually spent for inducing eddy currents. The developed equations describe non-equilibrium phonon population in semiconductor near the nanocontact as comprising two components: equilibrium and ballistic parts. The ballistic flow partially transfers its momentum to charge carriers (i.e. produces phonon drag), which results in electric polarization and eventually – in generation of the thermoelectric voltage. Numeric calculations showed that the effect is non-linear with respect to heat flux and contact size. The predicted phenomenon can possibly be used to develop thermoelectric converters with unique parameters.

articleTitle: Method for Improving the Performance of Operational Amplifier with HA2700 Microchip Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: A circuit technique for increasing the maximum output voltage slew rate (SR) of an integrated operational amplifier (OpAmp) with the HA2700 microchip architecture based on the modernization of the input differential stage (DS) is considered. An OpAmp architecture is proposed in which the influence of parasitic capacitances of DS reference current sources and capacitances on the transistor substrate on the SR is minimized. This allows the use of micron technological processes in the fabrication of CBJT OpAmps, which are widely used to improve the radiation resistance of microchips. Computer simulation of the proposed OpAmp is performed, which shows that the SR of the new circuit differs from the SR of the well-known serial OpAmp by more than 40 times and reaches values of about 800 V/µs at the emitter current of the input transistors of the DC in the range of up to 80-100 μA. The developed OpAmp is recommended for practical use in discrete-to-analog filters on switched capacitors.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation for 5G NR Communication System based on OpenAirInterface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: With the freeze of 3GPP Release 15 protocols, the world has entered the 5G commercial era. In recent years, major communication companies and organizations have set up project groups for IMT-2030 to put forward proposals on the 6G consideration of ongoing development, in which case the existing 5G new radio technology needs to be thoroughly verified. This paper, based on the software-defined radio (SDR) open source platform OpenAirInterface (OAI), provides a laboratory verification platform for 5G NR to evaluate the system performance in typical channel models. It provides a straightforward and flexible way of verifying the connectivity effect between the 5G core network (5GC), next Generation Node Base station (gNB) and User Equipment (UE) by visualization means such as software oscilloscopes.

articleTitle: Damage Accumulation in Alpha Gallium Oxide during Sequential keV Light Ion Implantations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: We present the results of investigation of radiation damage accumulation in α-Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> during sequential co-implantation with fluorine and phosphorous ions having different energies. It is found that both the amount and depth distribution of the resulting damage depend on the sequence of the implants. The mechanism of such non-commutativity is discussed in the framework of possible chemical effects.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Bandpass Filters by Transfer Function Using the Darlington Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This work is devoted to the implementation of filters by transfer function. The Darlington method was used to synthesize filters. This method has shown good accuracy of the frequency response. Butterworth, Chebyshev, and Kauer filters were selected for synthesis. The modeling of BPFs (bandpass filters) was performed in a Micro-Cap circuit simulator.

articleTitle: Effect of Asymmetrical Coating by Ald on Lagp Solid Electrolyte
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In this work, the effect of the coating on the properties of a solid electrolyte of composition Li1+xAlxGe2−x(PO4)3 was studied. Aluminum oxide coatings were applied by the ALD method. It was found that the use of the coating significantly increases the life of the solid electrolyte by protecting the surface from reaction with lithium.

articleTitle: Influence of the Bending of the Outer Mirror in the External Fiber Fabry-Perot Interferometer on the Interference Signal Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The basics of a simple analytical model of the EFPI interference signal, taking into account the bending of the outer mirror of the interferometer, are developed. The consideration uses a Gaussian beam model and a paraxial approximation using a ray transfer matrix. Simple approximate expressions for the Gaussian beam parameters are obtained taking into account the small ratio of the cavity length L and the curvature radius of the mirror RM. Calculations have shown that the influence of bending can be significant with sufficiently large, but practically possible L/RM ratios.

articleTitle: Algorithms for Using Ground Stations in Satellite Geolocation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper proposes algorithms for determining the location of a radio emission source (RES) using one, two, and three ground stations (GS). A mathematical description of these algorithms is provided, along with the results of data processing using these algorithms. The accuracy of satellite geolocation is presented as a result of these algorithms' work using each of them.

articleTitle: Effect of 3D-Substitutional Atoms on the Magnetic and Magnetostrictive Properties in (Tb,Ho)Fe2 Laves Phase
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The crystal structure, magnetic and magnetostrictive properties of the Laves phases Tb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.16</inf>Ho<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.84</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2-x</inf>T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> (T = Co, Ni, x = 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4) are investigated. Polycrystalline samples were prepared by induction melting with subsequent homogenizing annealing. The studied compounds crystallize in a structure of the MgCu2 type. Partial substitution of iron by Co and Ni leads to a decrease in the parameter and volume of the unit cell by ~3%. The Curie and spin reorientation temperatures of the studied compounds were determined, magnetic phase diagrams were constructed. Compounds with high values of saturation magnetostriction and magnetostrictive susceptibility in the temperature range of 190-320 K were found.

articleTitle: Modeling the Thermomechanical Behavior of a Bimorph Microcantilever Near Solid-Liquid Phase Transition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Infrared technology plays a pivotal role in numerous applications that permeate our daily lives, including motion sensors, fire detection systems, ear thermometers, and thermal imaging devices. The operational temperature range is a critical parameter for thermal detectors, particularly those deployed in elevated temperature environments. This paper investigates the variation in thermal properties of one of the two materials used in these detectors within a specified temperature range. The study presents a calculation of the resulting displacement amplitude due to changes in thermal properties and proposes a corresponding equivalent electrical circuit to model the system.

articleTitle: Error Oriented Tau Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: An effective approach to produce an approximate analytical solution to a linear ordinary differential equation with polynomial coefficients, is considered. This approach is a modification of the Tau method of C. Lanczos, however, it minimizes an error of the solution, not a residual of the equation. The effectiveness of the approach is illustrated by a numerical example. Other similar approaches are discussed briefly.

articleTitle: Public Dataset for Simultaneous Human Activity Recognition and Localization using WiFi Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: WiFi-based human sensing technology has unique properties such as widespread availability, resistance to light interference, overcoming terrain limitations, and respecting user privacy. It has been utilized in various fields. One interesting application is simultaneous human activity recognition and localization. However, CSI dataset collection is labor-intensive and affected by hardware requirements and timing synchronization between transmitters. Therefore, datasets are not publicly released in some studies. Other studies used a cable for timing between transmitters which limits the practicality in real-world scenarios. In this study, we release the first public dataset with wireless timing synchronization, WiARL-UIT, for simultaneous human activity recognition and localization. Finally, we have evaluated the performance of various machine learning models. As a result, the best accuracy is 97.0% when a convolutional neural network (CNN) model is used, showing the feasibility of the research direction of simultaneous human activity recognition and localization. The dataset and source code are publicly shared at https://github.com/F4tt/WiARL-UIT.

articleTitle: Numerical Study of the Dependence of the Parameters of Lensed Optical Fibers on Geometric Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This article presents a comprehensive study on the dependence of key parameters of lensed optical fibers on the geometry of the lens and the diameter of the fiber core. Lensed fibers, which have microlenses at their ends, are crucial in integrated and fiber optics for enhancing the efficiency of radiation input/output into optical integrated circuits, laser diodes, and photodiodes. The study focuses on the impact of the lens's radius of curvature and the fiber core diameter on the mode field diameter (MFD) and the focal length of the lens. Numerical experiments were conducted using the COMSOL Multiphysics 6.2 program, which allows for the design, analysis, and testing of photonic components by solving Maxwell's equations using the finite element method. The investigation involved various types of fibers, including UHNA1, UHNA3, and standard single-mode fibers (SMF 9/125), with core diameters ranging from 1.8 μm to 9 μm. The results show that the MFD and focal length are significantly influenced by the lens's curvature radius and the fiber core diameter. For UHNA fibers, which have thinner cores, the lens is effective only at small curvature radii, and its focusing capability diminishes at larger radii. In contrast, SMF 9/125 fibers maintain their focusing capability even at larger curvature radii. These results are crucial for optimizing the design of lensed fibers for various applications, including fiber-optic communications, biomedical imaging, and laser systems, where efficient light coupling and precise focusing are essential.

articleTitle: Application of Distributed Acoustic Sensors Based on Optical Fiber Technologies for Infrastructure Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This article discusses methods for applying Distributed Acoustic Sensors (DAS) based on optical fiber technologies in infrastructure monitoring systems. Acoustic sensors detect vibrations, noise, and other mechanical changes along the infrastructure, enabling real-time monitoring. The use of this technology helps in the early detection of infrastructure defects, allowing for preventive measures to be taken and reducing maintenance costs. The article highlights the capability of extracting and analyzing important information from noisy signals using signal processing techniques such as Fourier transformation. This approach is presented as a modern solution to enhance infrastructure safety and ensure its long-term and reliable operation.

articleTitle: Emitter of Accelerated Neutral Atoms and Molecules with Ion-Electron Conversion for Terrestrial Testing And Modelling of Spacecraft
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The article discusses the issues of modeling and laboratory testing of a low-orbit spacecraft flight in the ambient residual gas environment. To create conditions in a vacuum test facility for terrestrial study of spacecraft, close to those of flight, was developed an emitter of a radiating flow of fast neutral atoms and molecules with Ion-Electron conversion. The emitter device based on I) corona discharge in atmospheric air or special prepared gas at the first-time stage, and II) ion acceleration at the second time stage, and III) ion resonant recharging in the own gas at the third time stage. This module is supposed to be combined in the form of a complex with a large-volume vacuum chamber, with the help of which ground testing and modelling of spacecraft are carried out.

articleTitle: Conductive and Tensoresistive Properties of Flexible Polymer Compositres: Experimental Study and Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In this paper, we present the experimental results on the conductive and tensoresistive properties of polymer composites containing a small amount of carbon nanotubes. The experimental results on the resistivity dependence on the mass fraction of the CNT filler were analyzed within the classical percolation model. The sensitivity of the resistivity of synthesized composites with different mass fractions of the CNT filler to the degree of their uniaxial tension in a wide range of the applied strain was experimentally investigated. All obtained results were successfully described based on statistical percolation and resistive network models taking into account the influence of stretching on the curvature of carbon nanotubes.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of Iterative Demodulator of Coded SEFDM-signals with Higher-Order Modulation Subcarriers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper addresses the transmission and reception experiment of spectrally efficient frequency division multiplexing signals (SEFDM) reception with high-order modulation methods on subcarriers using NI USRP 2920. An iterative demodulation algorithm in conjunction with message-passing decoder for NR LDPC codes is utilized to demodulate coded SEFDM-signals. Spectral and BER performances of SEFDM-signals with QPSK, QAM-16 on subcarriers at various code rates are considered. In comparison with the results of the simulation, the experiments show approximate results of no more than 0.2 dB energy loss at BER = 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">–5</sup> and QAM-16 on the subcarriers. The experimental model allows flexible change of the signal designs and parameters depending on the requirements of various tasks.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Analysis of the Diode-Connected Transistor Mixers Using Volterra Series: Generalized Matrix Approach in the Frequency Domain
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The article is a sequel to the research devoted to the frequency mixers analysis based on generalized matrix approach in the frequency domain. This research investigates the nonlinear characteristics of diode-connected transistor mixers through the application of Volterra series, specifically balanced, double balanced, and triple balanced mixer configurations. An analytical algorithm is proposed to assess the nonlinear distortion caused by the third harmonic. The results encompass both theoretical calculations and simulations performed in Cadence Design Systems.

articleTitle: PAPR Reduction using Probabilistic Method for DVB-S2X with FTN Signaling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The purpose of this work is to evaluate the effectiveness of a probabilistic method for reducing PAPR of FTN signals generated based on the DVB-S2, DVB-S2X standards. Simulation model was created based on the lower layer of the scrambler from the DVB-S2X standards. Based on the results obtained, the gain from using the probabilistic method of reducing PAPR was assessed according to the level of the complementary cumulative distribution curve equal to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>. As a result, by increasing the symbol rate by 25% and using the probabilistic method with 16 scrambling sequences for PAPR reduction, the gain in PAPR is up to 1.4 dB compared to the case of orthogonal transmission for the DVB-S2X standard.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Nanostructured Ag and Ag-Cu Alloy Thin Films
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In the present work, thin alloy films of pure silver and silver-copper (Ag-Cu) have been deposited by DC magnetron co-sputtering at room temperature on silicon substrates. The elemental composition is determined by Rutherford backscattering spectrometry (RBS). X-ray diffraction (XRD) spectra of the deposited thin films confirm the formation of alloys. The films were further annealed in an inert (Ar) atmosphere at 200, 400 and 600 °C for one hour each. Nanoparticles are formed on the surface after annealing, as confirmed by field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) images. The size of the nanoparticles increases with annealing temperature. Nanostructured alloy films of Ag-Cu have various plasmonics based applications. They are more durable due to their immunity to oxidation. Moreover, the tunability of surface plasmon resonance in alloy films adds to their versatility.

articleTitle: Photoinduced Absorption Spectrum of GeSi/Si Quantum Dots in the Mid-IR and Terahertz Ranges under Resonant and Non-resonant Optical Pumping
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Vacuum Fourier spectrometer was used to obtain mid-infrared photoinduced absorption spectra of undoped GeSi/Si quantum dots at liquid helium temperature under different conditions of interband optical pumping. High-intensity peaks in the absorption spectra are associated with intraband hole transitions from the ground and excited states of the quantum dot to the continuous spectrum. The less intense long-wavelength peak corresponds to the hole transitions between the ground and excited states. In the terahertz spectral range, equilibrium absorption spectra were obtained, associated with transitions from the ground to a nearby excited state of holes. Structures with GeSi/Si quantum dots can be used to develop detectors of mid-infrared radiation.

articleTitle: Research on Laser Lift-off Process of Flexible OLED Panels for Phototherapy Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This study focuses on laser lift-off process in the phototherapy flexible OLED manufacture and its impact on devices. This article mainly analyzes the challenges faced by the current laser lift-off process of phototherapy flexible OLED panels, analyzes its effects on the luminous uniformity, luminous intensity and reliability of phototherapy flexible OLED panels from the aspects of laser type, laser energy, polyimide type and sacrificial layer, and finally gives the process verification results. Based on the experimental verifications of different types of lasers, scanning methods and substrates, the laser lift-off process yield up to 88% is proposed, which provides the possibility for the effective production of high quality phototherapy flexible OLED panels.

articleTitle: Synthesis and Properties of Heat-Resistant Polyimide Foams based on Various Diamines
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Based on esterified dianhydride of 3,3',4,4'-benzophenonetetracarboxylic acid using 4,4'-diaminodiphenylmethane and 4,4'-diaminodiphenyl ether, foaming prepolymers and polyimide foams were synthesized. A comparative study of the thermal and mechanical properties of polyimides obtained with various diamines was conducted. The synthesized foams have high heat resistance (the onset of weight loss is observed at 510°C); density varies from 8 to 12 kg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>; elastic modulus is 39-105 kPa.

articleTitle: Obtaining Thin Films from Semiconductor Compounds and Their X-Ray Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In this work, formation of thin layers of metal oxide, semiconductor compounds (BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and CaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) in the EPOS PVD DESK PRO magnetron sputtering device in radio frequency mode, their amorphous and crystalline phases, structural structure and optical properties were studied.Initially, BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> thin films were formed by radio frequency magnetron sputtering from a circular barium titanate target with a diameter of 76.2 mm. The X-ray phase analysis of the BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> compound was determined and the dispersion spectrum has a refractive index of 2.4 at a wave number of 821.68 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>. As a result of processing the spectra obtained using an infrared spectrophotometer, it was determined that the band gap of the semiconductor compound is 3.15 eV. The X-ray and infrared absorption and transmission spectra of CaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> powder, which belongs to the perovskite family, were analyzed, and one of the urgent tasks is to prepare a target for radio frequency magnetron sputtering. In the electronic industry, these perovskite compounds can serve as a valuable additive to improve various memory elements and dielectric layers of solar cells.

articleTitle: Formation, Phonon Structure, Transport and Thermoelectric Properties of Multilayer Heterostructures Si/NC β-FeSi2/Si/ NC β-FeSi2/…/Si(111) and Si/NC α-FeSi2/Si/ NC α-FeSi2/…/Si(111)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Multilayer (4 and 8 layers) samples with embedded β-FeSi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and α-FeSi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanocrystals (NCs) on silicon-on-insulator (SOI) substrates with (100) orientation and p-type conductivity have been grown. It has been established from Raman data that β-FeSi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> NCs are formed with small portions of iron (0.5 nm) deposited at room temperature and annealed at T = 630°C with subsequent overgrowing with silicon, and α-FeSi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> NCs are formed after short-term annealing at T = 1000°C and overgrowing with silicon. The effect of doping of intermediate silicon layers on the conductivity and Seebeck coefficient in multilayers (4 and 8) in the temperature range of 80–450 K was studied. It was shown that with maximum doping of intermediate layers (1019 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>) with the number of layers equal to 8, the maximum Seebeck coefficient 600 μV/K and the maximum power factor 2.5 mW/(m×K2) were observed at T= 450 K, which is due to the contribution of injected holes from β-FeSi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanocrystals.

articleTitle: FBMC/OQAM with OTFS Pre-Processing for High-Mobility Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a new promising modulation technique called Filter-Bank Multi-Carrier with Offset Quadrature Amplitude Modulation and OTFS Pre-processing (FBMC/OQAM-OTFS) for future mobile systems. We compared the effectiveness of the proposed modulation method to others such as OFDM, OTFS, and FBMC/OQAM in terms of the shape of the signal spectrum, the bit error ratio (BER) curves in standard channel models EPA, EVA, and ETU with maximum values of the Doppler frequency ranging from 5 to 3000 Hz, and the computational complexity of signal generation.
