Simulation results show that the proposed modulation technique provides a very low great out-of-band emission (OOBE) level like FBMC/OQAM (for overlapping factor K = 4 it is 112.3 dB lower compared to OFDM and OTFS), and 0.7–5.6 dB gain in energy efficiency a gain in energy efficiency about 0.7–5.6 dB in considered standard channel models compared to OFDM and FBMC/OQAM. However, the computational complexity of FBMC/OQAM-OTFS is still very high (about 14 times higher than that of OFDM), but it can be reduced by 3 – 4 times by applying a poly-phase structure.

articleTitle: Stresses in Ion Exchange Hardened Cylindrical Active Elements of Lasers based on Neodymium Phosphate Glasses
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Modelling and non-destructive diagnostics of residual stresses in cylindrical athermal neodymium active elements (AEs) of lasers are carried out: GLS 1715, hardened by low-temperature ion exchange Na<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> (glass) ⟺ K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> (melt) and aluminosilicophosphate GLS 817, hardened by low-temperature ion exchange Na+, K+ (glass) ⟺ Cs+ (melt). We also carried out a reconstruction of the radial distributions of axial stresses in AEs.

articleTitle: Calculation of SIW Structure Parameters Using Asymptotic Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper presents the results of the substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) investigation using the Poisson summation formula. The calculation on the representation of the conductors included in the SIW as separate cylindrical conductors of small radius. Three cases were considered: a single conductor, one array of cylindrical conductors at a fixed distance from each other, and two similar arrays at a fixed distance from each other. A simulation of the SIW structure in the ANSYS (Engineering Simulation Software) was also carried out.

articleTitle: Design and Realization of a Flexible Wearable Non-Invasive Phototherapy Device
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Non-invasive phototherapy is a non-invasive, painless, non-toxic, safe and effective photomedicine method that stimulates the organism through light irradiation and produces a series of physiological and biochemical reactions, which plays a role in repairing or regulating the physiological functions of the tissues or the organism so as to achieve the purpose of treating diseases. At present, non-invasive phototherapy has shown great potential in the prevention and treatment of joint degenerative diseases such as Osteoarthritis (OA) and neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's Disease (AD). However, the existing non-invasive phototherapy instruments are large, expensive, require professional operation and other problems, and patients need to go to the hospital for long-term treatment and other problems, which greatly increase the economic and time costs of patients. Moreover, LED is not flexible and generates high heat, requiring the addition of heat dissipation components, which cannot fit well with the skin. OLED light-emitting devices can be directly prepared into a surface light source on a flexible substrate, which itself is characterized by thinness, high flexibility, precise conformability, low power consumption and low heat generation, which is more suitable for clinical applications. In this paper, a wearable non-invasive phototherapy device based on flexible OLED is designed, which is characterized by flexible and thin, low power consumption and low heat generation. In addition, a driving scheme with precisely adjustable OLED luminous brightness, power is designed to determine the required optical dosimetry for optimal therapeutic effect.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Fault Isolability in Multi-Agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper analyzes the isolability of faults in networked systems, modeled as multi-agent systems where agents exchange information, forming a graph-like structure. We begin by examining the isolability of various fault types, including sen- sor faults, actuator faults, and faults in the connections between agents. We then present necessary and sufficient conditions that offer specific criteria for assessing fault isolability in the system, along with results for some particular cases. Finally, numerical examples are provided to validate our findings

articleTitle: Combination of 5G Broadcast and DVB-I Technologies for Unified Access to TV Services
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: 5G Broadcast is technology that provides opportunities for broadcast and multicast delivery of TV services to mobile devices. The paper describes possible ways for unified access to broadcast and unicast TV services at 5G mobile devices using DVB-I technology. The opportunity for combination of 5G Broadcast and other types of TV delivery networks is also considered.

articleTitle: Modeling the Influence of Magnetic Field on the Parameters of Onboard Rubidium Atomic Clocks Shield
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper presents the results of modeling the effect of an additional magnetizing field on the parameters of the shield of an onboard rubidium atomic clock. On a laboratory setup, under conditions of the effect of a rotating magnetic field on the clock, simulating the magnetic environment on satellite board, the dependences of the Allan deviation of the rubidium atomic clock frequency were obtained. The studies were carried out for different values of the magnetizing field oriented coaxially and perpendicularly to the optical axis of the clock. The parameters of the magnetizing field for the amplitude of the rotating magnetic field of 2.4 A/m, 4.8 A/m and 24 A/m, corresponding to high, medium and low orbits of satellites, were specified. Also, a numerical modeling of the magnetic field effect on the parameters of the atomic clock magnetic shield was performed, showing the efficiency of using the magnetizing field in low geomagnetic fields. Calculations of the shielding factor of a single-layer magnetic shield in the function of a magnetizing magnetic field are carried out and a close correspondence of this dependence to the dynamics of the longitudinal shielding coefficient measured in a model experiment with a two-layer magnetic shield of an atomic clock is noted.

articleTitle: Formation of Barium Silicide Coatings by Vacuum Thermal Evaporation Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Options for the formation of thin films of BaSi silicide are the method of vacuum-thermal evaporation of materials, in particular thermal evaporation from a directly heated boat and from a crucible with electronic heating. It was found that Si and other coating components evaporate relatively easily from a graphite crucible. Research has determined the possibility of obtaining BaSi coatings; their composition and structure have been studied, as well as the possibility of protecting it from atmospheric influences with a thin Cr coating.

articleTitle: Multicolor Dual-Layer Electrochromic Device
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper discusses the creation of multi-color electrochromic devices using two different electrochemical materials deposited on one electrode without intermediate layers using the example of a pair of NiO and Prussian blue. Stable and reversible operation of such a device with separate switching of each of the electrochromic materials was demonstrated. Electrochemical characteristics were studied using the сyclic voltammetry method.

articleTitle: Reduction of Mutual Influence and Losses in Antenna Matching Unit Coils
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Power amplifier matching with antenna is necessary to improve transmitters’ efficiency and output power. Among the problems that arise during the operation of the antenna matching device, we can highlight: mutual influence of inductance coils, the interaction of inductance coils with the shield or case, as a result of which insertion losses appear, and the frequency response of the matching circuit is distorted. These phenomena lead to a decrease in the efficiency of the antenna matching device. The paper discusses the design options for the antenna matching device with solenoidal and toroidal coils, as well as their interaction with the shield from the point of view of improving operational characteristics.

articleTitle: Development and Optimization of Distributed Acoustic Sensors for Seismic Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This work is focused on the development and optimization of distributed acoustic sensors for seismic monitoring. The study examines the structural features of the sensors, their installation, and application methods. Algorithms and methods designed for accurate detection of seismic events and real-time data processing are analyzed. Additionally, optimization methods used to enhance the efficiency of the sensors are explored. The results of this research are significant for the early detection of seismic hazards and the improvement of monitoring system reliability.

articleTitle: Effect of Agglomeration of Nanoparticles in Ferrofluid Induced by a Focused Laser Beam
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In the work, we discovered and investigated a number of phenomena associated with the influence of laser radiation on nanoparticles of ferrofluid (a colloidal material, the solid magnetically ordered phase of which is magnetite). It was found that the optical force acting on nanoparticles from the area of the focused light leads to the formation of various structures in the sediment of this substance when it is deposited on a substrate. These or similar phenomena can play an important role in various photonics devices.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of a CNN-Based Channel Estimation for OFDM Systems in High-Mobility Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Next-generation intelligent transportation systems demand communication technologies that deliver low latency and high reliability. However, a significant challenge for wireless communication systems is channel estimation in high-mobility scenarios. Thanks to the innovation of computer science, numerous applications of machine learning, particularly deep learning, in wireless communication systems are deployed to handle more diverse obstacles of the future mobile networks. Recently, deep learning-based channel estimations for wireless applications have garnered lots of attention from both researchers and industry. Among these efforts, a novel convolution neural network (CNN)-based channel estimation approach named ChannelNet was proposed for OFDM systems. ChannelNet treats the channel response matrix in the time-frequency domain as 2D images then the deep image processing techniques are used to enhance the intelligibility and reliability of channel estimation. Inspired by this reason, this paper gives a brief study of the abovementioned technique with the performance evaluation and comparison with current existing channel estimation techniques in high-mobility scenarios.

articleTitle: Raman and IR Spectrum Analysis of CrSi2 Thin Films Formed in Direct Current and Variable Frequency Modes of a Magnetron Sputtering Device
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: CrSi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> thin films were deposited using direct current and variable frequency magnetron sputtering. The formation of nanofilms by solid-phase ion-plasma method in high vacuum using a magnetron sputtering device in different modes is currently the most effective method. Chromium disilicide thin films were formed on SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> substrates and n-type Si(111) single crystals via magnetron sputtering in different modes, and performed spectroscopic analyses to determine their optical parameters. Before the deposition, the substrates were cleaned with acetone and ethanol in an ultrasonic bath for 5 min and dried under nitrogen (N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>). Thermal treatment of thin films was carried out in a dynamic vacuum (10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup> mbar) at a temperature of 750 K for 1 hour with a heating rate of 450 K·h<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> and natural cooling. The temperature was controlled by a K-type thermocouple next to the sample.Raman spectroscopy performed on polycrystalline thin films revealed the presence of a Raman-active mode at 508 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>. This confirms the density-functional theory calculations predicting a mode at 297 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, which has so far been difficult to observe in polycrystalline CrSi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. Combinatorial vibrations, one of the broad features centered at 1322 and 1563 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, were also observed.

articleTitle: The Emission Characteristics and Electron Energy Distribution Function of a Novel Composite Field Cathode Prototype
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This manuscript comprises the novel experimental, numerical and theoretical investigation results for a newly developed low-macroscopic-field emission cathode prototype. The brief introductory information regarding the baseline for both scientific and engineering background is provided. The prototype acquisition process is described. Scanning electron microscopy images of the material surface are included. The results of emitted electron energy spectra modeling based on WKB approximation considering the formation of charged states with negative correlation energy values, correspond well to the acquired experimental data. Each of the observed peaks relates to the specific "hot electron" energy levels emerging due to the existence of the potential-well structure within the cathode surface layer.

articleTitle: ECG Monitoring System Based on Multi-Scale Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper introduces the Multi-Scale SEEnhanced Convolutional Network with Atypical Pre-Activation (MSE-CNet-AP), a novel model for a multi-lead ECG signal recognition. The proposed system applies a multi-scale network with attention mechanisms to enhance spatial feature extraction from ECG signals, which are then used for classification. The proposed system uses a single-board computer as a hardware part, and facilitates real-time ECG data acquisition and classification, achieving a 96.40% identification accuracy, highlighting its clinical potential.

articleTitle: Planar Micropillar Cavity Structure with Enhanced Power-Conversion Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: We present the results on the modelling and fabrication of micropillar cavity structure with enhanced power-conversion efficiency. The use of Al0.2Ga0.8As/Al0.9Ga0.1As pairs in the mirrors of a micropillar cavity allows to increase the power-conversion efficiency at 130 K by more than 11 times compared to the cavity design with Al0.9Ga0.1As/GaAs mirrors. This microcavity structure was grown by molecular-beam epitaxy. The microcavity structure grown by molecular-beam epitaxy had the resonance energy of about 1.29 eV at the center of the epi-wafer, and the energy has been shifting by about 11 meV along the radius of 3-inch wafer. The root mean square of surface roughness was less than 0.4 nm.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of High Tc Superconducting Charge-Based Qubit
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Quantum computing has advantages over conventional computing in performing algorithms such as factorization and search. Quantum processors, as a tool for quantum computing, are computing units that consist of qubits as basic elements. There are different approaches toward the implementation of the qubits. The most renowned and applicable of these implementations is based on superconducting qubits. Among various types of superconducting qubits, charge qubits in form of transmons are chosen in this work because of their straightforward fabrication methods and better interfacing and scalability. In this paper, utilizing EPR (Energy Participation Ratio) method, one of the main transmon structures made of High T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> superconductor materials, are designed and simulated. Additionally, the effects of some geometry-based parameters of the qubit structure on qubit characteristics such as frequency and anharmonicity are explored. Moreover, the single transmon qubit structure with High T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> superconductor transmission lines as readout and control sections are designed and simulated. In addition, due to the Purcell effect, the Purcell filter is added to the designed single qubit structure to reduce the spontaneous emission of the qubit. The results of our simulations are compared with that of the conventional superconductor based transmons.

articleTitle: Collision Reduction Methods and Decollision Processing Algorithms in the Space Segment of AIS
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In the AIS satellite monitoring system, the key problems are the presence of message collisions and Doppler frequency shifts of received signals, which greatly affects the degradation of signal detection quality. This paper considers ways to reduce the probability of message collisions and methods to combat and resolve collisions in the event of their occurrence. The paper studies the efficiency of various non-coherent detection algorithms under the above-described conditions. Joint application of decollision processing algorithms is considered. An increase in the probability of correct detection and demodulation of colliding signals has been demonstrated. In addition, a study was conducted on the influence of the orientation of the antenna system to reduce the probability of collisions occurrence.

articleTitle: MIMO-NOMA Analysis. Part II. Power Allocation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This study is devoted to the characteristics of MIMO systems with non-orthogonal multiple access. In this part of the study, the method of cluster formation as well as the method of power allocation among user equipments (UEs) in the cluster, required for the subsequent superposition coding procedure, are discussed.

articleTitle: Joint Application of Signals With Controlled ISI and Iterative Decision-Feedback Detection Algorithm in DVB-S2
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: the paper considers the application of signals with controlled ISI in the DVB-S2 standard. An iterative processing algorithm with decisions feedback used together with the error-correcting coding defined in the standard. The possibility of increase in transmission rate shown with permissibly small losses in energy efficiency. In addition, for some parameters of the symbol transmission rate and code rate, it is possible to achieve an increase in energy efficiency with a fixed bandwidth efficiency. The results given for two extreme cases of possible signal constellations defined by the standard - QPSK and 32APSK.

articleTitle: Water Indicator Measurement and Data Processing From Internet of Things Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This article presents the results of the implementation of a measuring system based on an IoT module for remote transmission of aggregate measurement data obtained during analytical monitoring of five water parameters via a wireless communication channel. A model of an experimental setup is presented and discussed, demonstrating the operability and consistency of the model for monitoring physical parameters during aggregate measurements. The obtained results of remote data transmission via a wireless communication channel revealed a statistically significant correlation between spring water parameters and the most influential predictor of acidity, conductivity, turbidity and oxidation-reduction potential is water temperature. The discovered relationship between the measured parameters is mainly associated with the effect of temperature on the processes occurring with an increase and decrease in the temperature of the analyzed water samples.

articleTitle: Hardware Implementation of Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Nowadays neural networks become very useful in different fields of research such as image recognition, optimization, data analysis, classification and prediction tasks. Though, increasing complexity leads to longer calculation time and higher power consumption, what constrain using of neural networks in different types of applications. This makes a reason to develop specific hardware implemented circuits for neural networks. This paper briefly reviews present possibilities and approaches of hardware implementation for some types of neural networks.

articleTitle: Scenarios for Use of DVB-I System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: DVB-I technology provides opportunities for aggregation of TV services from different types of delivery systems (Terrestrial, Satellite, Cable, IPTV, OTT and Mobile TV). The paper considers scenarios for possible deployment of this system and highlights the benefits of this system for broadcasters, network operators, manufacturers and TV viewers.

articleTitle: Hardware-Software Prototyping of a Multichannel Frequency-Modulated Continuous Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: A hardware and software module of the FMCW radar based on the AWR1243BOOST prototyping board from Texas Instruments has been developed and implemented. It allows implementing the full range of functions of the AWR1243 radar chip. The results of experimental testing of the radar for measuring the range, speed and angle of the target are presented, confirming the possibility of creating prototypes of modern FMCW radars.

articleTitle: Oscilloscope and Arbitrary Waveform Generator 3D Interfaces for a Virtual Reality Remote Laboratory
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Remote laboratories proved their effectiveness during the COVID-19 pandemic and since then have been a convenient tool to support the educational process. The addition of virtual reality makes remote laboratories as close as possible to work in the real laboratories. This paper presents the results of developing of 3D interfaces of the Rigol DS1054z oscilloscope and Rigol DG822 arbitrary waveform generator in virtual reality for integration into an existing remote laboratory to transform it into a virtual reality remote laboratory.

articleTitle: Antenna Module with Integrated SIW Passband Filter for Application in Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper presents an antenna module with an integrated microwave filter built on a multilayer printed circuit board (PCB) with the use of substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology. It consists of a triple-layer cavity resonator with coupling irises and a slot antenna edged on the top layer of a structure. This module is designed to operate in the Long Term Evolution (LTE) Band7 frequency band with a 70 MHz bandwidth. The module can be easily implemented into antenna arrays any configuration with frequency and polarization diversity due to its high isolation and good suppression of out-of-band radiation. The proposed filtering antenna is fabricated and tested. Simulation and measurement results with close agreement between them are presented in this letter. The maximum measured gain of the prototype is 3.64 dBi at 2.655 GHz. A novel technique of fabricating SIW filtering antenna is described. The synthesis methodology for filtering antennas is also proposed.

articleTitle: Improved Quenching Circuit for a Single Photon Detector with Avalanche Photodiode
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper deals with the problem of quenching the avalanche breakdown (AB) in avalanche photodiodes (APD) operating in Geiger mode and used in single photon detectors (SPD). The paper describes the problem of AB events that are sometimes missed by traditional quenching circuits (QC) and proposes an improved QC. Comparison of traditional and improved QCs in a real hardware is presented, showing the benefits of the improved circuit.

articleTitle: Design of a Slot Phase Shifter Using a Radio-Frequency Microelectromechanical Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Based on the existing waveguide-slot phase shifter design, an improved method is introduced to achieve better simulation results using RF MEMS switches. The performance of phase shifters utilizing RF MEMS switches is compared with those using p-i-n diodes. The results demonstrate that the phase shifter with RF MEMS switches provides more evenly spaced phase shifts across the frequency range of 8.5-10.5 GHz, avoiding phase overlap, which is a limitation observed in p-i-n diode-based phase shifters. This highlights the enhanced phase control and system efficiency achieved with RF MEMS switches.

articleTitle: An Inverse Problem of Differential Equations of Non-linear Oscillations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: With the help of presented algorithm based on the non-linear method of least squares it is possible to find the unknown values of parameters that are components of differential equations whose solutions could be used for adequately modeling oscillations of non-linear systems in radiophysics, electronics etc. The input data of the algorithm are the experimental data on time dependences of said oscillations. The novelty is in study of the case when the differential equations have no analytic solutions and can be solved only numerically.

articleTitle: Improving Energy Efficiency of Single-Frequency Signals in Industrial Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Wireless communications in industrial scenario is complicated due to severe multipath propagation which causes significant signal distortions at receiver. Application of complex equalizers and error correcting codes is not appropriate since it limits the battery life of industrial devices. In this paper, the optimization problem with the constraint on the level of signal distortions caused by multipath propagation was formulated. An industrial channel was simulated in Matlab with the use of raytracing. The obtained optimal pulse provides reduction of signal distortion level by more than 80% compared to root raised cosine pulses.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Beta-Active Carbon Nano-Layer Using Ion-Plasma Technology for Irradiated Reactor Graphite Deactivation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In this paper we present ion-plasma deactivation technology for the decontamination of irradiated reactor graphite and the simultaneous extraction of the dose-forming isotope <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup>C in the form of a useful product – a beta-active nano-layer. Ion-plasma deactivation technology is based on the using of a “short” discharge in an inert gas environment (argon) and allows for the compact extraction of the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup>C isotope from the surface of RBMK reactor graphite blocks. The extraction of the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup>C isotope is carried out by processing graphite blocks in in argon “short” discharge in, namely by argon ion sputtering of the graphite blocks surface layer enriched with <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup>C isotope. Operating parameters of ion-plasma technology: pressure 0.1-1 atm., voltage 200-1000 V, discharge current 0.001-1 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, discharge gap 0.1-3 mm. The deposition of the sputtered layer of 14C is realized in the diffusion mode on the metal electrode-collector surface in the solid form. The fabricating of solid deposit containing the isotope can be used, for example, in nuclear medicine and for the creating of beta-voltaic batteries based on the beta emitter isotope <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup>C. In our experiment, deposited carbon layers (beta-active nano/microlayer) of different thicknesses were obtained on nickel electrode collector during the process of sputtering reactor graphite at different plasma discharge exposure times. Extracted <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup>С isotope can be used for the fabrication of beta-active layer inside of "nano-micro-sandwich" for the manufacturing of “eternal” energy sources – a new vacuum-beta-cell (VBC).

articleTitle: Influence of Ultraviolet Irradiation on the Formation of Surface Holographic Structures Recorded in a Counter-directional Recording Scheme on Photoemulsion Layers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The possibility of using the Denisyuk counter-directional optical scheme for recording holographic relief-phase gratings on the silver halide photoemulsion PFG-01 is investigated. It is shown that the key operation leading to the formation of the surface relief of the grating in a wide range of spatial frequencies of 35 – 800 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> is the irradiation of the photoemulsion with short-wave UV radiation with a wavelength less than 270 nm. It is found that the greatest values of the diffraction efficiency of the obtained holographic gratings in the region of the highest spatial frequencies of 550 – 800 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> are achieved when using undiluted glacial acetic acid as an etchant for gelatin.

articleTitle: 180° Reflection-Type Phase Shifter Using GaAs pHEMT Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The results of reflection type phase shifter (PS) monolithic integrated circuits study are presented. Considered PS provides 180° phase shift and operates in 7 – 11 GHz frequency range. The investigated PS are made in the form of microwave monolithic integrated circuit (MMIC) based on the 0.5μm GaAs pHEMT technology. Phase shifter circuits are designed using Lange couplers. Studies of various variants of folded Lange coupler topology were carried out to reduce the MMIC chip size. It was shown that coupler topology modification allows to decrease PS dimensions more than twice with insignificant deterioration of its frequency responses. Comparative phase shifter characteristics allowing to rationally choose PS circuit are given.

articleTitle: Low-Pass Filters with Pseudo Resistors for Electronic Stethoscopes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This article is devoted to the design of a low-pass filter for an electronic stethoscope using pseudo resistors. A filter with imitation of inductors by an active circuit based on operational amplifiers with a bandwidth of 1 kHz has been chosen as a low-pass filter. Ripples in the bandwidth are 0.9 dB, and the stopband attenuation, starting at 10 kHz, is 77 dB. The efficiency of the filter is simulated at various temperatures and corner parameters. The values of nonlinear distortions and noise characteristics have been found, as well as the dynamic range of the filter equal to 44 dB, power consumption is 293 μW. The filter layout has been designed with an area of 68 000 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. It is possible to significantly reduce the filter chip area while maintaining acceptable filter characteristics, due to the use of pseudo resistors.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling of IPMC Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The study is devoted to the development of an easily modifiable and visual mathematical model of a sensor based on ionic polymer-metal composites (IPMCs), requiring a small number of empirically found coefficients. The physics of the IPMC sensor operation and the provisions justifying the creation of a model of the processes inside the polymer ion-exchange membrane are reviewed. The developed model allows considering the frequency dependence of the IPMC sensor output signal on external mechanical action, predicts the signal amplitude under various external impacts, describes the stabilization time of the output voltage at a constant pressure on the working body. In order to reduce the technical requirements for the computer, the original mathematical model was simplified, replacing the calculation of hydrodynamics with an empirical coefficient, but a full implementation of the model is planned in the future.

articleTitle: Obtaining Nano-Sized Silicide Films MESi2 for the Contact System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Using the method of implantation of Ba<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> ions in combination with heating, a barrier layer was created between the contacting metal Cu and silicon. It has been shown that the formation of a BaSi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> barrier layer with a thickness of ~100 A leads to a decrease in the depth of diffusion of Cu into the BaSi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Si system by up to 5–6 times, and does not exceed more than 110–120 Å. The results of a study of the current-voltage characteristics of the system's current-voltage characteristics showed that good ohmic contact when irradiating the system with a light flux is maintained up to Φ ≈ 1000-1000 lux.

articleTitle: Study of SDR-Based Direction Finder Threshold Sensitivity Depending on Signal-To-Noise Ratio
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper presents the effect of a radio direction finding system based on software-defined radio. The implemented software and hardware system investigates the stability of bearing calculation for searching for radio emission at different levels of signal/noise ratio. The obtained results show stable determination of bearing levels up to 5 dB. In the process of the study, a study was conducted using a microwave generator, which acted as a source of radio emission. The obtained direction finder allows to significantly reduce the cost of the direction finding system, as well as to ensure high accuracy of determining the characteristic in the 80-degree sector. The obtained results are presented in the form of tabular results, as well as graphs of the dependence of the average measured bearing error on the signal/noise. The proposed direction finding system can be easily implemented due to the use of an open SDR system, printed antenna manufacturing, and additive manufacturing of the direction finder component.

articleTitle: Numerical Researching the Modal Structure of Gallium Phosphide Microresonators
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In this work numerical calculation of the modal structure of gallium phosphide nanowires is performed. Simulation results showed that raise in diameter leads to the increase in the number of optical modes having different light distribution due to transverse mode type. Quality factor analysis shows growth in its values with the increase in structures’ diameters.

articleTitle: PIC Design for the Two-Channel Dual-Band SS-OCT System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper presents the design of the photonic integrated circuit (PIC) for the dual-band swept-source optical coherence tomography (SS-OCT) system. The designed PIC includes two interferometric schemes for the 820-880 nm and 1260-1360 nm wavelength ranges and optical triggers for both schemes. We developed PIC for the silicon nitride platform because it provides lower losses than other integrated photonics platforms. We made design verification with numerical simulation in the Ansys Lumerical software.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of High-Speed Methods of Frequency Measurement of the Power Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: There are many digital methods for measuring the frequency of the power grid. The main disadvantage of all existing methods is the long time required to perform measurements, which complicates their use in modern control systems and control tasks that require getting a quick result. In mentioned areas, a group of so-called "fast" measurement methods is used, the most outstanding of which are the method of three samples and the method of the second derivative of the input signal. This publication provides a comparative analysis of these methods. The causes of static and dynamic measurement errors under sinusoidal and non-sinusoidal input signals are considered. It is shown that the main cause of error is the difference between the input signal shape from the sinusoidal one. For the measurement method based on the second derivative of the input signal, options for constructing digital differentiators are considered. The effect of the differentiator on the frequency measurement error under sinusoidal and non-sinusoidal input signals is estimated. For the least squares method, the accuracy of calculating the number of samples is given, the result for ensuring high measurement accuracy while maintaining low time. Methods for reducing errors are considered and their effectiveness is assessed using simulation modeling in Matlab/Simulink.
